troubleshooting.problem: Marinade blackens before the slices finish.

substitutions.alternative: Scallion-pepper pork with hoisin and sriracha
substitutions.effect: For the original 1.5 lb pork-tenderloin batch, keep 1/4 cup fish sauce, 1 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp sugar; replace the 3 minced garlic cloves and 2 lemongrass stalks with 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves, 6 sliced scallions (white and tender green parts) and 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper. Puree this marinade, toss with the thinly sliced tenderloin and refrigerate 2–4 hours. Scale those alternative amounts with the full recipe. Choose 6 rolls about 8 inches long for the original batch, or the listed baguettes cut into serving lengths, in place of the main bread allocation. Use hoisin and sriracha, unmeasured as wanted, instead of mayonnaise and liquid seasoning; use 1/2 seedless cucumber cut into matchsticks and 1 1/2 loosely packed cups cilantro sprigs for the original batch, scaled proportionally. Carrot-daikon pickles and jalapeños are not required by this route. Use a separate unmeasured grilling-oil allowance for grates and brushing the pork; grill uncrowded skewered slices over high heat with about 4 minutes total as a first check, turning and watching the sugars. Reach the same 145°F endpoint and three-minute rest, and remove skewers before serving. This route has different aromatics, toppings, heat and portion planning.

after.timing: Allow about 3 hours with the minimum 2-hour refrigerated marinade: about 30 minutes sandwich preparation, grill setup, roughly 10 minutes cooking for the original batch and a 3-minute cooked rest. The linked pickle’s 20-minute preparation plus at least one hour chilled can run during marination. Extra grill loads, thicker slices, the actual grill setup and overnight marination extend elapsed time.
after.storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F, at 40°F or below. Use within 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F throughout. Store pork separately from bread and cold toppings. Use the linked pickle’s own storage guidance; assemble sandwiches near serving, since dressed bread loses texture.

sources.title: Luke Nguyen — Grilled Pork Banh Mi

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Banh mi sandwiches are Vietnamese street food defined by contrast: grilled pork against pickled vegetables, cilantro, and creamy mayo on crusty bread. The marinade is garlic, fish sauce, and brown sugar - a workhorse base that caramelizes on the grill. The pickled vegetables are non-negotiable: they're the cooling, cutting element that makes the sandwich balanced.

## Directions

1.  **Marinate:** Whisk fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic, and lemongrass. Toss with the pork. Let marinate for at least 2 hours (ideally overnight).
2.  **Pickles:** Prepare your [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon) while the pork marinates: allow about 20 minutes for cutting and packing, then at least 1 hour in the refrigerator before serving. Keep them refrigerated until assembly.
3.  **Grill:** Thread pork onto skewers or use a grill basket. Wipe off excess marinade and grill over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and just cooked through.
4.  **Assemble:** Split the baguettes. Spread a generous layer of mayo. Drizzle with a few drops of liquid seasoning or soy sauce.
5.  **Fill:** Layer the grilled pork, cucumber spears, [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon), and fresh cilantro. Top with jalapeños for heat.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Bánh mì sandwiches bring grilled pork, crisp bread, cool pickled vegetables, cilantro and creamy mayonnaise together. This lemongrass version uses the listed sugar and honey with fish sauce and garlic; a medium grill helps keep the sweet coating from blackening. Drain the pickles for assembly so they brighten the filling without soaking the bread.

## Directions

1. **Marinate the pork cold:** Have pork tenderloin or pork butt, fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic cloves, and lemongrass stalks ready. Whisk the full fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic and lemongrass supply together, then toss with all the thinly sliced pork. Cover and refrigerate at 40°F or below for at least 2 hours, or overnight. Keep the entire batch coated and use enough covered food-safe vessels for larger batches.
2. **Prepare the pickles:** If not prepared ahead, make the linked [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon) while the pork marinates: allow about 20 minutes cutting and packing, then at least 1 hour in the refrigerator. Keep them refrigerated until assembly; choose the serving amount separately rather than assuming the full pickle recipe is used.
3. **Grill the thin pork:** Thread the pork onto suitable skewers or use a grill basket, following the equipment’s preparation instructions. Use suitable grilling oil as needed for the cooking surface. Lift the pork from the marinade and wipe away excess; discard the raw-contact marinade. Grill uncrowded slices over medium heat, starting checks around 3–4 minutes per side, until browned without blackening and at least 145°F in the thickest part, measured from the side with a thermometer suitable for thin food. Pork butt and tenderloin can differ in chewing texture; neither is guaranteed finished by the clock. Keep waiting raw pork refrigerated and add grill loads as needed.
4. **Rest cooked pork:** Transfer fully cooked pork to a clean platter and rest at least 3 minutes before assembly. Use clean utensils and remove any skewers before eating.
5. **Assemble and serve:** Use crusty baguettes, [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon), fresh cilantro, jalapeños, cucumber spears, mayonnaise, and liquid seasoning or soy sauce. Split the measured bread, spread generously with mayonnaise and add a few drops of liquid seasoning or soy sauce. Divide all the cooked pork among the serving lengths; layer cucumber, drained chilled pickles and cilantro, then jalapeños if wanted. Serve promptly. Four portions is the current original-batch plan, not a measured baguette-size yield.
